purpose: Check that MCTS search depth buys strength on the coarse-to-fine candidate path, by playing one model against itself at two playout budgets. Both seats share a single evaluator, so the comparison isolates search from policy quality. The legacy candidate path is measured at the same settings as a control.
notes: Search scales on the coarse path: 92.5% at 8x budget and 81.0% at 2x budget, both with confidence intervals clear of 0.5. The coarse->fine sampler is not blocking depth from converting into strength.

At 8x the two paths are statistically indistinguishable (coarse 92.5%, legacy 94.2%, overlapping intervals on 80 games). At the harder 2x ratio the coarse path scores higher (81.0% vs 72.5%), but those intervals also overlap, so this run does not establish a scaling advantage on its own.

The legacy 2x control is the weakest measurement here: 9 of 80 games hit the ply limit and were excluded, leaving 71 completed and an average of 100.7 plies against a 160 limit. Truncation censors exactly the games the deep seat was grinding out, so 72.5% is a floor rather than a clean estimate. Rerun at a higher --max-plies before treating the coarse-vs-legacy gap at 2x as real.

At equal simulation counts the coarse path is consistently faster and more decisive: 224.7s vs 412.2s at 8x and 783.8s vs 1236.8s at 2x, with far shorter games (33.4 vs 54.6 plies at 8x, 69.3 vs 100.7 at 2x) and fewer truncations (0 and 1, against 2 and 9). Legacy games drift toward the ply limit.
Geometry must match the training run. Driving this model at the default radius 1/6 instead of 1/18 puts the raster out of distribution and inference returns NaN.
Games are colour-swapped in pairs and truncated games are excluded from the score, so `completed` rather than `games` is the denominator.
